tools.name: create_session
tools.description: Open a new empty file in a visible GenOffice tab and start an editing session; family picks the editor: docx (Word document), pptx (presentation), xlsx (spreadsheet). Then add content with that family's tools (docs: insert_content / replace_blocks / apply_ops; slides: apply_slide_ops; sheets: apply_sheet_ops) and finish with save_session. One session is active at a time — a new create_session replaces it. The user watches each step in the app.

tools.name: save_session
tools.description: Save the active session to an absolute path and end it. A path with no extension gets the active family's file format appended (docx: .docx; xlsx: .xlsx; pptx: .pptx); a different extension is refused. Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite is true. This is the output step.

path.description: absolute output path for the file

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing file at `path`; default false

tools.name: read_docx
tools.description: Read a Word .docx file and return its visible text (one paragraph per line).

tools.name: open_in_genoffice
tools.description: Open an existing file in the running GenOffice app, focusing its tab.

path.description: absolute path to the file to open

tools.name: get_app_info
tools.description: Report GenOffice version, the default save folder, the document formats this server can generate, and the editor's full open/save/export format matrix per family.

tools.name: insert_content
tools.description: Insert content into the visible document as HTML (headings, paragraphs, bold/italic, lists, tables, links). Appends at the end unless afterBlockIndex is given.

afterBlockIndex.description: insert after this block index; default appends at the end

tools.name: replace_blocks
tools.description: Replace a range of blocks in the visible document with new HTML content. Use read_document to learn block indexes.

html.description: restricted HTML fragment the range is replaced with

tools.name: apply_ops
tools.description: Apply formatting commands to the visible document (font, paragraph format, heading level, find/replace, list/indent, etc.). `ops` is the same batch format the built-in AI editor accepts; the whole batch is atomic. Use read_document for block indexes.

dryRun.description: validate and plan the batch without changing the document

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: Read the visible document: its blocks with indexes, text and current formatting, so you can target follow-up edits.

tools.name: read_deck
tools.description: Read the visible presentation: every slide with its elements (ids, types, text, geometry) so you can target follow-up edits. Element ids and slide indexes are what apply_slide_ops addresses; geometry is document-space EMU (1 px = 9525 EMU on a standard 16:9 deck).

tools.name: apply_slide_ops
tools.description: Apply slide editing ops to the visible presentation as one transaction (atomic by default, plan-validated with snapshot rollback; per_op isolation skips failures instead). Ops address {slide, el} and use document-space EMU. Common ops: setText, setFont, setParagraphFormat, addElement (textbox/shapes/lines), addTable, addChart, addBlankSlide, deleteSlide, moveSlide, duplicateSlide, deleteElement, setFill, setStroke, setTransform, setBackground, applyTheme, findReplace, setTableCell, tableStructure, setTransition, setNotes. A failing atomic batch changes nothing — fix the op named in the error and resend the whole batch. Use read_deck for ids and geometry first.

ops.description: array of op objects (at most 50 per transaction)

isolation.description: atomic (default) applies all-or-nothing; per_op applies independently

dryRun.description: validate and plan the batch without changing the deck

tools.name: read_sheet
tools.description: Read the visible workbook: sheet names/ids with data extents, and optionally the current values/formulas of specific cells. Sheet ids and A1 addresses are what apply_sheet_ops targets.

addresses.description: A1 addresses to read (values + formulas); omit to get the workbook overview only

sheetId.description: sheet to read from (id from a previous overview); default is the active sheet

tools.name: apply_sheet_ops
tools.description: Apply workbook DSL operations to the visible spreadsheet (the same vocabulary the built-in AI uses). Common ops: set_cell, set_formula, clear_cell, set_range, clear_range, fill_range, copy_range, convert_to_values, insert_rows, delete_rows, insert_cols, delete_cols, add_sheet, delete_sheet, add_chart, add_table, set_filter, set_hyperlink, add_conditional_format, set_data_validation, set_note. Addresses are A1 on the target sheet. One batch applies as one undo step; a failed batch changes nothing. Use read_sheet for sheet ids and current values first.

ops.description: array of workbook DSL op objects

dryRun.description: plan the batch and report what would change, without modifying the grid
